basic_identification.sector_category: Footwear (approved by the Chemical Division Council and finalized by the Footwear Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard specifies the requirements, methods of sampling, and test procedures for polyvinyl chloride (PVC) industrial boots manufactured by injection molding or other molding processes. These boots are designed to protect workers' feet in demanding industrial environments (such as chemical processing plants, construction sites, and agricultural applications) from water, acids, alkalis, physical impacts, and slip hazards.

version_status_and_amendments.edition_year_of_copy: Second Revision, 2021 (incorporating Amendment No. 1 and Amendment No. 2, November 2024)

amendment_slips.description: Updates physical-mechanical parameters and aligns select testing routines with revised BIS footwear guidelines.

Substitutes Clause 5.5.5 to mandate that slip-resistance must be evaluated in accordance with Clause 5.5 of ISO 4643 (replacing the legacy Annex B of ISO 4643). It also completely replaces Clause 5.11.1 to update minimum sole thicknesses when tested per IS 15298 (Part 1), enforcing separate minimum boundaries for forepart and heel thickness with (d1) and without (d2) cleats.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Footwear made from All Rubber and All Polymeric Material and its Components (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, all Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) Industrial Boots must carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, stocking, or selling uncertified boots in the Indian market is a statutory offense. Micro and small enterprises (MSEs) are granted specific delayed implementation schedules, and export-only shipments are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to molded polymeric protective footwear.

requirements.detail: Each boot must be legibly and indelibly marked on the outer waist of the sole and the inner face of the upper with the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's licence number (CM/L).
The boots are classified into two designs based on shaft height: Type 1 (Ankle Boots) and Type 2 (Gum Boots / Wellington Boots / Wellington Gumboots).

The standard establishes three varieties based on toe protection: a) Variety 1: Safety footwear (fitted with a steel toe cap designed to withstand high impact energy of 200 J and 15 kN compression load); b) Variety 2: Protective footwear (fitted with a steel toe cap to withstand medium impact energy of 100 J and 10 kN compression load); c) Variety 3: Occupational footwear (manufactured without steel toe caps for general protective wear).

When tested in accordance with IS 15298 (Part 1), the sole thickness must satisfy the following limits: a) Forepart: d1 (thickness including cleats) must be minimum 6 mm, and d2 (thickness excluding cleats/sole base) must be minimum 4 mm; b) Heel: d1 (thickness including cleats) must be minimum 9 mm, and d2 (thickness excluding cleats) must be minimum 6 mm.
Boots must satisfy strict slip-resistance parameters on wet and slick industrial floorings. Under Amendment No. 2, the test must be performed in accordance with Clause 5.5 of ISO 4643.
Molded boots must possess robust bond strength: the upper-to-outsole joint must satisfy minimum peel resistance limits to prevent splitting or delamination under continuous bending.
Every boot must undergo an inflation leak-proofness test, demonstrating zero air bubble escapes when submerged in water under a specified internal pressure.
The raw plasticized PVC compound must show low plasticizer loss under heat aging, exhibiting high volatility control when tested in accordance with IS 12240 (Part 4).

Boots must meet strict baseline thresholds for: tensile strength and elongation at break of the PVC upper, flexing resistance (Ross flex cyclic testing), outsole abrasion resistance, tear strength, and hardness.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 12254 : 2021 is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification governing polyvinyl chloride (PVC) industrial boots (gumboots and ankle boots) utilized for personal protection in factories, mines, chemical plants, and construction sites. Under the national Footwear Quality Control Order (QCO), all such PVC industrial boots sold, distributed, or imported in India must bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). The standard divides boots into Type 1 (Ankle) and Type 2 (Gum Boots), and establishes three varieties based on whether they contain safety steel toe caps (resisting up to 200 J impact). Amendment No. 2 (November 2024) enforces strict new sole thickness parameters—demanding distinct minimum forepart (min 6 mm with cleats, min 4 mm base) and heel (min 9 mm with cleats, min 6 mm base) limits—and updates the slip-resistance criteria to align directly with international ISO 4643 benchmarks to protect workers from catastrophic slips and physical injuries.
